Date: 2026-08-22

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, uh, argus lane activation — I'm Samir, AE on the account, with dana and owen from our success and eng teams. how's everybody doing?
[00:05] Marta: good, thanks. we've been looking forward to this. quick context: we need a private deployment, cannot have any tokenized data leaving our VPC, and we have a compliance window for september.
[00:12] Priya: and to add, we need cert evidence for SOC two controls, ke--- key management integration, and we operate with an HSM-backed KMS for critical keys.
[00:20] Samir: ok, yes. so Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS — we integrate with mainstream providers and there is an HSM path. uh, caveat: some of the older quantized runtimes have slight differences in how keys are loaded, we'll make sure security sees the notes.
[00:31] Owen: (interrupts) one quick thing — when you say private, do you mean the full private control plane or the VPC peered variant? sometimes customers want the private control plane and sometimes they want dedicated capacity behind a peering.
[00:40] Ethan: we're leaning toward VPC peering into your hosted control plane for now, to avoid ops overhead. main requirement is egress restrictions and retained audit logs for 3 years.
[00:49] Dana: sounds reasonable. we can do VPC peering; we'll send a template for the peering config and recommended CIDR ranges.
[00:55] Jonah: question — how do you handle KV cache persistence? we have a lot of short-lived sessions, worried about cache thrash and perf.
[01:02] Owen: great question. our runtime uses a per-request KV cache with optional prefix caching for repeated prompts; for high-concurrency workloads we suggest continuous batching and we can tune max tokens per batch. some of that is tuned in the model profile.
[01:15] Marta: ok, we need measurable goals — like 99th percentile under 200ms for small prompt paths and baseline cost per 1k tokens. can those be measured in pilot?
[01:23] Samir: yes, pilot is exactly for that. we'll run a benchmark script against your staging VPC with representative QPS and measure p50/p95/p99 and cost per token with the same tokenization the app uses.
[01:30] Priya: also, SSO — we run Okta with SCIM provisioning; we need role based access controls mapped to Okta groups.
[01:36] Dana: SAML SSO + SCIM is supported, yes. we can wire RBAC to Okta groups and propose least privilege roles. I'll put together the mapping table.
[01:43] Ethan: network specifics — do you need NAT egress? we have a strict egress proxy, TLS intercept, etc.
[01:48] Samir: for peering, the control plane will talk back over the peering; if you have outbound firewalling we need to allow certain endpoints and ports. we'll send the full egress list. if you have TLS intercept that will break mTLS with our agent, so we need to discuss a bypass for the control-plane traffic.
[02:05] Priya: right, TLS intercept is a blocker for mTLS. we can create allowlists but need justification and evidence.
[02:11] Owen: note — sometimes the transcription and the product names come out wrong in these notes; i said 'Redwood Dedicated' earlier but we meant the peered private option. apologies for noise in the logs.
[02:21] Marta: timeline check — we have a compliance demo to leadership in mid-september, can we show a pilot by first week of september?
[02:28] Samir: yes targetable. with VPC peering and if the staging VPC is provisioned this week, we can schedule a 48-hour pilot the week of aug 31 or sept 7.
[02:36] Jonah: cadence during pilot — would you do canary model rollout or a single version?
[02:40] Owen: pilot normally runs on a pinned model artifact to reduce variance; we can do A/B if you want to compare quantized vs fp16. but recommend pinned single model for baseline.
[02:49] Ethan: and cost — if we spike QPS in pilot, will that blow up our bill? we need burst caps or rate-limits.
[02:55] Dana: there are burst policies we can set in Dedicated and peered setups; for pilot we'll propose a cap and also provide simulated token cost estimates in the benchmark report.
[03:05] Priya: audit logs — we need immutable logs forwarded to our splunk instance and retention for three years. can you stream audit events?
[03:11] Samir: yes. we can stream audit events over our log forwarder, or provide an S3 export — both options possible. for long retention we usually recommend S3 + lifecycle policy to your archive bucket.
[03:20] Marta: encryption at rest — want confirmation of envelope encryption and KMS key rotation practices.
[03:26] Owen: we use envelope encryption; keys are stored in customer KMS when using private deployment with customer-managed keys. key rotation is supported and we'll share the doc on rotation mechanics.
[03:34] Random: [crosstalk — some voices overlap]
[03:40] Samir: ok i'll summarize next steps — dana will send the SSO mapping template and network template, owen will build the pilot script, and i'll share the terraform snippet for peering and example security integration notes.
[03:51] Ethan: small note — we use a custom egress proxy that rewrites certs, that will probably require a bypass as priya said. we'll triage with infra folks.
[03:58] Priya: i'll send a short note of the mandatory controls for SOC2 and an initial list of evidence.
[04:05] Samir: great. any other blockers?
[04:08] Marta: none from me. one more ask — can we have our SREs get a quick runbook to troubleshoot latency spikes?
[04:14] Owen: yes, we'll include an SRE runbook and a troubleshooting checklist for common KV cache and batching issues.
[04:21] Dana: scheduling — i'll send a calendar invite for the pilot kickoff and include a 2-hour window for onboarding and tests.
[04:26] Samir: perfect. thanks everyone.
[04:30] Marta: thanks.
[04:33] End of recording.
